messages:
jun: quick design review: form patterns for the Organization > API Keys flow. two things I want to settle: required-field UX and destructive confirmation CTA phrasing.

devin: for required fields I'm leaning toward using an explicit legend at the top: "Fields marked * are required" + mark required inputs with an asterisk visually and aria-required="true". avoids forcing '(optional)' everywhere.

maria: +1 on the legend, but prefer marking optional fields with '(optional)' instead of marking required ones. that reduces visual noise for forms where most fields are required. also it helps for screen reader clarity.

own: accessibility tradeoff: screen reader users will encounter the legend either way, but aria-required is important. also ensure the asterisk has sufficient contrast (not light gray).

jun: good notes. what about inline validation timing? should we validate on blur, on submit, or both?

devin: blur + submit. avoid validating on every keystroke for non-deterministic checks (eg server-unique slug). show optimistic inline hints while typing for format rules (e.g., regex sample), then validate on blur.

maria: when we show inline errors after submit, we should also show a concise error summary at the top with a link list to each field. example copy: "We couldn't save this form. 2 fields need attention." then bullets. focus the summary (move keyboard focus) and use role="alert" so it's announced.

own: implementation note: set aria-invalid="true" on the input elements with errors and include aria-describedby pointing to the inline error element. that makes each error discoverable for AT users.

access-bot: Accessibility reminder: ensure error color contrast >= AA, and do not rely on color alone; include iconography or text.

jun: destructive confirmation copy: current modal text is bland. proposal: make consequence explicit and require typed confirmation for high-impact deletes. sample: 

```
Title: Remove dedicated capacity pool "gpu-reserve-01"?
Body: Removing this pool will immediately stop all running jobs and cannot be undone. Type the pool name to confirm.
Confirm CTA: Remove "gpu-reserve-01" (danger)
Cancel CTA: Keep pool
```

jun: thoughts on CTA placement? left vs right primary.

devin: follow our platform convention: destructive primary on the right (red), cancel on the left. keeps keyboard flow consistent. ESC closes.

maria: microcopy nit: prefer specific verbs: 'Remove' vs 'Delete' depending on domain language. stick to one verb across the console. if we use 'remove' for pools, use it everywhere for pools.

own: small UX suggestion: if resource is shared, include a brief list of dependent resources (eg "3 running jobs") in the modal to make the consequence clearer.

jun: good call. final Q: should the confirm button include the resource name? pros and cons.

devin: include the resource name when we do typed-confirm or when there are ambiguous names. else optional. helps prevent mistakes.

maria: for keyboard accessibility, ensure modal traps focus and that the typed-confirm input receives initial focus. have live-updates of validity for the typed match but don't announce errors on every keystroke.

jun: action items: 1) maria will update Figma with legend vs optional-label variants; 2) devin will add modal copy examples and typed-confirm prototype; 3) owen will add an accessibility checklist (aria-required, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, role=alert, focus management).

maria: I'll add both patterns in a single frame so we can A/B test with PMs. link when ready.

own: I'll run keyboard-only through VoiceOver and NVDA once prototype exists.

access-bot: Checklist saved: [legend for required fields OR explicit '(optional)' labels, aria-required on required inputs, aria-invalid + aria-describedby for errors, role="alert" and focus move to top summary on submit, typed-confirm for high-risk deletes, include dependent-resource context].
